title: A variable with your name
brief:
The program already has two variables: name and age. Do not change them.

Print two lines using the variables, not by typing the values again:

```
My name is Karel.
I am 3 years old.
```

If you change the value of name later, your program should print the new name without any other change.

vocabulary.gloss: a name that holds a value, so you can use the value later
a whole number, like 3 or 42 (Python calls it int)
the data a variable holds, for example "Karel" or 3

starterCode:
name = "Karel"
age = 3

# Print the two lines below, using the variables

tests.name: prints exactly two lines
tests.expectedStdout:
My name is Karel.
I am 3 years old.

hints: print() can show more than one thing. Put a comma between them: print("My name is", name)
With commas, print() puts a space between each thing. To get the full stop right after the name, join the text with +: print("My name is " + name + ".")
age is a number, so you cannot join it to text with +. Either use commas — print("I am", age, "years old.") — or change it to text first with str(age).
solution:
name = "Karel"
age = 3

print("My name is " + name + ".")
print("I am", age, "years old.")
